Facts: Alluvial plain from Sadiya to Dhubri, annual monsoonal floods.[cite: 1]
Tributaries: Siku/Jiari, Gai, Jiadhol, Subansiri, Buroi, Borgang, Jia Bharali (Kameng), Gabharu, Belsiri, Dhansiri (North), Puthimari, Pagladiya, Manas, Tipkai, Sankosh, Raidak (Gadadhar).[cite: 1]
Sub-basin Notes: Ranganadi and Dikrong join the Subansiri network near the Brahmaputra; Beki and Aie act as significant sub-tributaries for Manas.[cite: 1]

Tributaries: Burhi Dihing, Disang, Dikhou, Jhanji, Bhogdoi, Dhansiri (South), Kopili, Kulsi, Krishnai, Dudhnoi, Jinjiram.[cite: 1]
Karbi Anglong & Dima Hasao, Meghalaya Plateau extension, Barail Range, and Haflong hill station.[cite: 1]
Features: Situated between the two valleys (Karbi Anglong and North Cachar Hills). Geologically, it is an extension of the Indian Peninsular Plateau (Meghalaya plateau).[cite: 1]
Significance: Comprises rugged terrains, the Barail range, and dense tropical forests. It is home to the state hill station, Haflong.[cite: 1]
Cachar, Hailakandi, Karimganj, tea gardens, Son Beel wetland.[cite: 1]
Tributaries (East to West): Jiri, Chiri, Madhura, Jatinga, and Larang.[cite: 1]
Cachar, Hailakandi, Karimganj, tea gardens, Son Beel wetland.[cite: 1]
Tributaries (East to West): Sonai, Rukni, Ghagra, Katakhal, Dhaleshwari, and Longai.[cite: 1]
Biodiversity Hotspots, WNHS (1985), Biosphere Reserves, 7 National Parks + Sikhna Jwhwlao NP (2025), Wildlife Sanctuaries, Bird Sanctuaries, and Deepor Beel Ramsar Site.[cite: 1]
Assam falls within two distinct global hotspots: the Eastern Himalayas and the Indo-Burma hotspot.[cite: 1]
Kaziranga National Park (1985) and Manas Wildlife Sanctuary (1985).[cite: 1]
Manas Biosphere Reserve (foothills) and Dibru-Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve (765 sq. km).[cite: 1]
Kaziranga NP (1974), Manas NP (1990), Nameri NP (1998), Dibru-Saikhowa NP (1999), Orang NP (1999), Dehing Patkai NP (2021), Raimona NP (2021), plus Sikhna Jwhwlao NP (2025).[cite: 1]

Key Wildlife Sanctuaries: Pobitora WS (Morigaon, highest density of one-horned rhino), Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary (Jorhat, India only ape - Hoolock Gibbon), Bornadi WS (Udalguri/Baksa, hispid hare & pygmy hog), Chakrashila WS (Dhubri/Kokrajhar, golden langur), Deepor Beel WS (Kamrup Metro, major Ramsar wetland site for water birds).[cite: 1]

Complete List of Sanctuaries in Assam: Amchang WS (Kamrup Metro), Borail WS (Cachar & Dima Hasao), Bherjan-Borajan-Padumoni WS (Tinsukia), Bura-Chapori WS (Sonitpur), East Karbi Anglong WS (Karbi Anglong), Garampani WS (Karbi Anglong, oldest & smallest), Laokhowa WS (Nagaon), Marat Longri WS (Karbi Anglong, biggest), Nambor WS (Karbi Anglong), Nambor-Doigrung WS (Golaghat), Pani Dihing WS (Sibsagar), Sonai Rupai WS (Sonitpur).[cite: 1]
Wetland Marvels: Son Beel (Karimganj, largest wetland in Assam), Chandubi Beel (Kamrup, natural earthquake lake).[cite: 1]
Project Tiger (4 Reserves) and Project Elephant (5 Reserves).[cite: 1]
Project Tiger (TR, 1973): Assam has 4 Tiger Reserves: Manas TR, Nameri TR, Kaziranga TR, and Orang TR.[cite: 1]
Project Elephant (ER, 1992): Assam has 5 Elephant Reserves: Kaziranga-Karbi Anglong ER (largest at 3,270 sq. km), Dhansiri-Lungding ER, Chirang-Ripu ER, Sonitpur ER, and Dihing Patkai ER.[cite: 1]
Assam acts as the transit hub for Northeast India with an extensive network of National Highways connecting all Seven Sister states.[cite: 1]
Key Highways: NH-27 (formerly NH-37) is the lifeline corridor traversing Assam east-west from Srirampur to Silchar/Sadiya.[cite: 1]
Connectivity: Bridges like Bhupen Hazarika Setu (Dhola-Sadiya) and Bogibeel Bridge connect crucial NH networks across the Brahmaputra River.[cite: 1]
Administered by the Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR) zone headquartered in Maligaon, Guwahati.[cite: 1]
Network: Extensive broad gauge railway tracks connect Upper Assam to Lower Assam and the rest of mainland India via the Siliguri Corridor.[cite: 1]
Landmark Projects: Bogibeel Bridge is the longest rail-cum-road bridge in India, providing seamless connectivity between north and south banks.[cite: 1]
National Waterway 2 (NW-2) comprises the Brahmaputra River running from Sadiya to Dhubri (891 km).[cite: 1]
National Waterway 57 (NW-57): Developed on the Kopili River, spanning 48 km from the Brahmaputra confluence to the Teliagaon Railway Bridge, operationalized in August 2025.[cite: 1]
Infrastructure: Pandu Port in Guwahati is the largest and most developed river port in Assam, serving as an inland water terminal.[cite: 1]
Logistics: Promotes eco-friendly and cost-effective bulk cargo trade connecting Northeast India to international ports via Bangladesh.[cite: 1]
